text: Continuous integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Every time a developer adds new code to a shared project, an automated build starts immediately. The system then runs a series of tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines make this process smooth and repeatable, so no step is forgotten. As a result, developers can fix mistakes quickly and release software more safely. In short, continuous integration saves time and improves quality by keeping the code healthy and reliable.
